# Design: Structural keywords recognized per language

## Context

Every structural keyword is a string literal today, spread over `codev-core`:

- `parser/shared.rs` — `section_header`, `delta_section_kind` (`ADDED` …
  `RENAMED` + `REQUIREMENTS`, ASCII case-insensitive), `requirement_header`
  (`### Requirement:`), `scenario_header` (`#### Scenario:`),
  `wrong_level_scenario` (`### Scenario:`);
- `parser/spec.rs` — `Purpose`, `Requirements` compared with
  `eq_ignore_ascii_case`;
- `parser/delta.rs` — `Purpose`, `unexpected_headings` (whose doc comment
  and message say the keyword "stays in English"), `find_labelled_line`
  (`Reason`, `Migration`), `parse_renames` (`FROM:`, `TO:`),
  `rename_target` (`### Requirement:`), `kind_label`;
- `validate/rules.rs` — `check_requirement_shall` (`contains("SHALL") ||
  contains("MUST")`);
- `merge/render.rs` — `"### Requirement: "`, `"#### Scenario: "`;
  `merge/mod.rs` — the `RENAMED` header rewrite and `build_new_spec`
  (`# … Specification`, `## Purpose`, `## Requirements`);
- `domains.rs` (`HEADING = "## Domains"`), `changelog/release_note.rs`
  (`HEADING = "## Release note"`, `"## What Changes"`), both through
  `parser/section.rs`, which matches a whole heading line.

The merge rewrites main specs by byte spans (`Span::byte_range`) and must stay
character-exact for everything it does not touch. Codes are declared in
`parser/codes.rs` and `validate/codes.rs`, and listed in
`docs/*/src/reference/file-formats.md`.

## Goals / Non-Goals

Goals:

- one place that knows the keywords, with `en` and `fr` entries;
- English files parse, validate and merge exactly as before;
- the merge writes headings in the main spec's keyword language.

Non-goals:

- localizing the templates, `codev instructions` or the skills — they keep
  serving English keywords;
- a user-defined catalog in `config.yaml`;
- translating identifiers (domain names, release-note categories, `None`) or
  the scenario step markers (`**GIVEN**` …), which codev does not parse;
- decision files.

## Decisions

### Decision: The catalog is static data in `codev-core`

A new module `codev-core/src/keywords.rs` defines a `Lang` enum (`En`, `Fr`)
and a `Keywords` struct holding every form of the spec's table: section
titles, requirement and scenario heading words, the four delta words and the
`Requirements` word with their order (`ADDED Requirements` vs
`Exigences AJOUTÉES`), removal labels, rename labels, normative keywords and
the three proposal section titles, plus the canonical rendering of each
heading (`"### Exigence : "`). `pub static CATALOG: &[Keywords] = &[EN, FR]`
and `fn keywords(lang: Lang) -> &'static Keywords`.

Every literal listed in Context is replaced by a lookup. The `EN` entry holds
exactly today's literals, which is what keeps English behavior unchanged.

It is pure data, so it belongs in the functional core (decision 0001), and
`codev-core` is the only crate every reader of keywords already depends on
(decision 0002).

**Alternatives considered**: a YAML catalog loaded at runtime — needs I/O in
the core or a port for read-only constant data, and makes the catalog a user
surface the proposal excludes; one catalog per crate — the parser, merge and
proposal readers would drift apart again.

### Decision: Matching folds case, French accents and the colon space, without a new dependency

A helper `keywords::strip_keyword(line, keyword) -> Option<usize>` walks the
original line and the keyword char by char, comparing them after lowercasing
and folding `à â é è ê ë î ï ô ù û ü ç` (and their capitals) to their base
letter, and treating ` :` like `:`. It returns the **byte length of the
matched prefix in the original line**, so the extracted name, the spans and
the heading prefix are always taken from the source, never from a normalized
copy — the byte offsets the merge relies on stay exact even though `É` is two
bytes and `E` one.

`delta_section_kind`, `requirement_header`, `scenario_header`,
`wrong_level_scenario`, `find_labelled_line`, `parse_renames`,
`rename_target` and the `Purpose` / `Requirements` comparisons all go through
it, trying each catalog entry in turn. They now return the `Lang` that
matched alongside today's result. A keyword whose normalized form is
identical in several entries (`**Migration**`) is reported as shared
(`None` language).

**Alternatives considered**: the `unicode-normalization` or `deunicode`
crate — a new dependency for a dozen characters, and normalization changes
byte lengths, which would leak into span arithmetic; exact matching on the
accented forms only — French keyboards outside France and copy-paste make
`AJOUTEES` common, and the spec requires both.

### Decision: The AST records the keyword language and the heading prefix

- `Spec` and `Delta` gain `keyword_language: Lang` — the language of the
  first non-shared structural keyword, `Lang::En` when there is none — and
  `foreign_keywords: Vec<(u32, Lang)>`, the lines of structural keywords
  in another language.
- `Requirement` gains `heading_prefix: String`, the source text of its
  heading up to the name (`"### Exigence: "`), so that `RENAMED` rewrites
  `heading_prefix + new name` and keeps the keyword exactly as written.

The parser collects these while it scans; it emits no finding for them.

**Alternatives considered**: re-detecting the language inside the merge from
the source text — a second scanner that ignores fences differently is how the
two would disagree; storing the name's byte range instead of the prefix —
equivalent, but the prefix makes the rename a one-liner.

### Decision: Rendering takes the target keywords explicitly

`render::requirement(req, kw: &Keywords)` and `scenario_str` use
`kw.requirement_heading` / `kw.scenario_heading`. `merge::merge_into_existing` passes
`keywords(spec.keyword_language)` for `ADDED` and `MODIFIED`;
`build_new_spec` passes `keywords(delta.keyword_language)` and also takes the
title pattern (`# <Title> Specification` / `# Spécification <Title>`) and the
two section titles from it. Descriptions and scenario bodies are copied as
today — never translated.

Idempotence is unaffected: the second sync finds the requirements by name,
which does not depend on the heading language.

**Alternatives considered**: rendering in the delta's language — the user
asked explicitly that the merge keep the spec's language, and a mixed main
spec would then trip `mixed_keyword_languages` after every sync.

### Decision: Mixing is a validator rule, not a parser finding

A new rule `MixedKeywordLanguages` in `validate/rules.rs` turns the first
entry of `foreign_keywords` into a warning `mixed_keyword_languages`
(declared in `validate/codes.rs`), for main specs and deltas. It reuses the
existing warning path, so `--strict` applies with no change. A delta and its
main spec are never compared for this rule.

`requirement_no_shall` checks `CATALOG.iter().flat_map(normative)` with the
same word-boundary behavior as today (`contains`), and its message lists
`SHALL`, `MUST`, `DOIT`. The `delta_unexpected_heading` message lists the
requirement headings of every catalog entry; the "stays in English" wording
and the doc comment of `unexpected_headings` go.

**Alternatives considered**: an error — a mixed file is still fully
understood, and blocking sync on it would punish a half-translated spec;
checking only the configured `language:` — the spec makes recognition
independent of configuration, so the warning must be too.

### Decision: Proposal sections are looked up by a list of headings

`parser/section.rs` gets `section_any(source, headings: &[&str])` and
`heading_line_any`, returning the first heading of the list found in the
file, in file order. `domains.rs` and `release_note.rs` replace their
`HEADING` constant by `keywords::proposal_headings(Section::Domains)` etc.
Domain names, categories and `None` are untouched.

**Alternatives considered**: a `## Domaines` alias hard-coded in
`domains.rs` — exactly the scattering this change removes.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [An English file parses differently after the refactor] → A golden test
  parses and syncs every spec under this repository's `_codev/specs/` and
  `_codev/changes/archive/` with the new code and compares with the output
  of the `en`-only literals captured in fixtures; the `EN` entry is the
  literal strings, reviewed against the list in Context.
- [A free-form `## Objectif` section in an English spec is now read as
  Purpose] → Only the first Purpose-like heading counts, as today; a later
  one stays a free section and raises `mixed_keyword_languages`, which
  points at it. Judged unlikely in an English spec.
- [Byte offsets wrong after an accented match] → `strip_keyword` returns
  original-byte lengths; unit tests cover `É` / `E`, ` :` / `:` and a
  multi-byte name, and a merge test rewrites a French spec and checks the
  untouched requirement byte for byte.
- [A project with French keywords used by a teammate on an older codev,
  which rejects `### Exigence :`] → The docs tell such projects to raise
  `codev_version:` in `config.yaml` to the release carrying this change;
  `codev doctor` and the skills already enforce it.
- [The skills still say a translated keyword is a broken artifact] →
  Accepted for now: what the skills write stays English and valid; the
  wording is revisited by the change that localizes templates.
- [`normative` matched with `contains`: `DOIT` inside a word] → Same
  behavior as `SHALL` / `MUST` today; uppercase-only `DOIT` makes accidental
  matches rare. Not tightened here, to keep English behavior identical.

## Migration Plan

Additive: no file format is removed and no JSON field changes. The only
visible differences for an English project are reworded
`delta_unexpected_heading` and `requirement_no_shall` messages. Rollback is
reverting the change; French specs written in the meantime would then fail
validation, which the `codev_version:` guidance prevents.

## Open Questions

- Which further languages to add — each is a new catalog entry and does not
  change this design.

# Proposal: Structural keywords recognized per language

## Why

A team that writes its specs in French must still type the structural
keywords in English (`### Requirement:`, `## ADDED Requirements`, `SHALL`…):
a `### Exigence :` is rejected by validation with `delta_unexpected_heading`,
and the English forms are hard-coded in the parser, the validator, the merge
and the proposal readers. Now that `language:` lets teams write their prose
in their own language, the structure is the last part they cannot.

## What Changes

- A built-in **keyword catalog per language** lists, for each language,
  the form of every structural keyword codev parses. It ships two
  languages: `en` (today's keywords, unchanged) and `fr`.
- Parsing recognizes the keywords of **every** catalog language, whatever
  `language:` says: `## Objectif` / `## Exigences`, `### Exigence :`,
  `#### Scénario :`, `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` / `MODIFIÉES` / `SUPPRIMÉES` /
  `RENOMMÉES`, `**Raison**` / `**Migration**`, `DE :` / `VERS :`.
  English files parse exactly as before.
- The `SHALL` / `MUST` rule also accepts the French normative keyword
  `DOIT`; the code `requirement_no_shall` is unchanged.
- The proposal sections codev reads — `## Domains`, `## Release note`,
  `## What Changes` — are also found under `## Domaines`,
  `## Note de version`, `## Changements`.
- Each spec file has a **keyword language**, the one of its structural
  headings. Validation warns (`mixed_keyword_languages`) when a file mixes
  the keywords of several languages.
- **Merge keeps the language of the spec it modifies**: the
  `### Requirement:` and `#### Scenario:` headings that a sync writes or
  retitles in a main spec use the keyword language of that main spec, not
  the delta's. A main spec created from a delta takes the delta's keyword
  language.
- `delta_unexpected_heading` still reports a heading no catalog knows; its
  message no longer says the keyword must stay in English, it names the
  accepted forms.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `structural-keywords`

### Modified Capabilities

- `spec-parsing`
- `spec-merge`
- `validation`

### Removed Capabilities

## Impact

- `codev-core`: new keyword catalog module; `parser/shared.rs`,
  `parser/delta.rs`, `parser/spec.rs`, `parser/section.rs`,
  `validate/rules.rs`, `merge/mod.rs`, `merge/render.rs`, `domains.rs`,
  `changelog/release_note.rs` read their keywords from the catalog instead
  of string literals.
- `codev-engine`, `codev-cli`: no new command, flag or configuration key;
  the JSON contract (`codev-cli::contract::v1`) is unchanged — only the text
  of some finding messages changes, and one warning code is added.
- Documentation: `guides/artifact-language.md` and
  `reference/file-formats.md`, in `docs/en` and `docs/fr`, list the French
  keywords and the merge rule.

Assumptions made without asking (evaluation run, no user available):

- The catalog is built into codev, not configurable in `config.yaml`;
  adding a language means adding an entry to the catalog in a later change.
- Recognition does not depend on `language:`: a project with `language: en`
  also accepts a French spec, so changing `language:` never invalidates the
  existing specs.
- The skills and templates keep writing English keywords, as the `skills`
  spec requires; serving templates in the configured language is a separate
  change.
- Values that are identifiers rather than structure stay in English: domain
  names (`security`…), release-note categories (`Added`…), and the line
  `None`.
- Keywords codev does not parse — `## Why`, `## Impact`, the design and
  tasks headings, `**GIVEN**` / `**WHEN**` / `**THEN**` — are already free
  text for codev and are not part of the catalog.
- French keywords are matched case-insensitively, with or without accents
  (`AJOUTEES` = `AJOUTÉES`), and with or without the space French typography
  puts before a colon (`Exigence :` = `Exigence:`).
- Decision files (`_codev/decisions/`) are out of scope.

## Domains

- [ ] security
- [ ] personal-data
- [ ] user-interface
- [ ] performance
- [ ] operations
- [x] migration — existing English specs must parse and merge identically; a new warning code appears in `codev validate --json`

## Release note

- Added: Specs and deltas can use French structural keywords — `### Exigence :`, `#### Scénario :`, `## Exigences AJOUTÉES`, `DOIT`… — alongside the English ones, and `codev sync` keeps the keyword language of the spec it modifies.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: A sync keeps the keyword language of the main spec it modifies

When a sync writes a requirement block into an existing main spec — for
`ADDED` or `MODIFIED` — it SHALL write the requirement and scenario headings
with the keywords of the main spec's keyword language, whatever the keyword
language of the delta. The description and scenario bodies MUST be copied
from the delta as written, without translation. A `RENAMED` SHALL replace
only the name in the existing heading, keeping its keyword as written.
Re-running the same sync MUST change nothing.

#### Scenario: English delta modifying a French main spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec whose keyword language is `fr`, containing a
  requirement `Connexion`
- **AND** a delta with `## MODIFIED Requirements` carrying
  `### Requirement: Connexion` and a `#### Scenario: Jeton`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the main spec carries the replaced block under the heading
  `### Exigence : Connexion`, with its scenario heading
  `#### Scénario : Jeton`
- **AND** the main spec contains no `### Requirement:` heading

#### Scenario: French delta adding to an English main spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec whose keyword language is `en`
- **AND** a delta with `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` carrying
  `### Exigence : Mode sombre`, whose description contains `DOIT`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the requirement is appended under the heading
  `### Requirement: Mode sombre`
- **AND** its description is copied as written, `DOIT` included

#### Scenario: RENAMED in a French main spec keeps the heading's keyword

- **GIVEN** a main spec containing the heading `### Exigence: Expiration`,
  written without a space before the colon
- **AND** a delta renaming `Expiration` to `Délai d'inactivité`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the heading becomes `### Exigence: Délai d'inactivité`
- **AND** the body and scenarios of that requirement are identical down to
  the character

#### Scenario: A second sync changes nothing

- **GIVEN** a French main spec already synced with an English delta
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>` again
- **THEN** the main spec is identical, down to the character, to what it was
  after the first sync

### Requirement: A new main spec takes the keyword language of its delta

When a sync creates a main spec for a new capability, it SHALL write the
spec's sections and headings with the keywords of the delta's keyword
language. A delta whose keyword language is `fr` MUST produce a spec whose
title is `# Spécification <Title>`, followed by `## Objectif` and
`## Exigences`; a delta in `en` produces the same file as before.

#### Scenario: New capability from a French delta

- **GIVEN** no main spec under `_codev/specs/theme/`
- **AND** a delta carrying `## Objectif` and `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` with a
  requirement `Mode sombre`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** `_codev/specs/theme/spec.md` starts with `# Spécification Theme`
- **AND** it contains the delta's Purpose under `## Objectif` and the
  requirement under `## Exigences`, headed `### Exigence : Mode sombre`

#### Scenario: New French capability without Objectif is rejected

- **GIVEN** no main spec under `_codev/specs/x/`
- **AND** a delta carrying only `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` without `## Objectif`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** no write takes place
- **AND** the error recalls the stable code `new_capability_without_purpose`

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: French main specs and deltas parsed like English ones

The parser SHALL extract the same structure from a file written with the
French keywords of the catalog as from its English equivalent: the Purpose
and Requirements sections of a main spec, each requirement with its name,
description and scenarios, and the four delta operations with their
payloads. A `DE :` or `VERS :` value MAY be the bare name or the heading
form in either language; both designate the same requirement. The parser's
structural defects MUST be reported for French keywords as they are for
English ones.

#### Scenario: French main spec

- **GIVEN** a file containing `## Objectif`, a sentence, then `## Exigences`,
  then a requirement heading `Expiration de session` written with
  `### Exigence :` and followed by a scenario `Inactivité` written with
  `#### Scénario :`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** the result exposes the Purpose text
- **AND** exposes a requirement named `Expiration de session` carrying its
  scenario named `Inactivité`

#### Scenario: French delta with the four operations

- **GIVEN** a delta containing `## Exigences AJOUTÉES`,
  `## Exigences MODIFIÉES`, `## Exigences SUPPRIMÉES` with `**Raison**` and
  `**Migration**` lines, and `## Exigences RENOMMÉES` with the lines
  `- DE : Ancien nom` and `- VERS : Nouveau nom`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** the result carries the `ADDED`, `MODIFIED`, `REMOVED` and
  `RENAMED` operations in that order
- **AND** the `REMOVED` operation carries its reason and migration
- **AND** the `RENAMED` operation associates `Ancien nom` with `Nouveau nom`

#### Scenario: RENAMED written with the French heading form

- **GIVEN** a delta containing `## Exigences RENOMMÉES` then the lines
  ``- DE : `### Exigence : Ancien nom` `` and
  ``- VERS : `### Exigence : Nouveau nom` ``
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** the `RENAMED` operation associates `Ancien nom` with `Nouveau nom`

#### Scenario: French scenario written with three hashes

- **GIVEN** a requirement whose scenario is written `### Scénario :` instead
  of `#### Scénario :`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** a structural defect reports the line and indicates that the
  scenario must carry four hashes
- **AND** the requirement still appears in the result, without that scenario

#### Scenario: French delta header in a main spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec file that mistakenly contains an
  `## Exigences AJOUTÉES`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** a defect reports the line and specifies that delta headers
  belong only in change files

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Localized structural defects

When faced with a malformed file, the parser MUST produce a report naming the
line concerned, the defect type, and a readable message; it SHALL NOT
fail wholesale on a partially recoverable file.

#### Scenario: Scenario written with three hashes

- **GIVEN** a requirement whose scenario is written `### Scenario:` instead of
  `#### Scenario:`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** a structural defect reports the line and indicates that the
  scenario must carry four hashes
- **AND** the requirement still appears in the result, without that scenario

#### Scenario: Duplicate requirement within the same section

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` delta containing two requirements with
  exactly the same name
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** a defect reports both lines of the duplicate requirements
- **AND** names the `ADDED` section as the location of the conflict

#### Scenario: Delta header in a main spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec file that mistakenly contains an
  `## ADDED Requirements`
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** a defect reports the line and specifies that delta headers
  belong only in change files

#### Scenario: Unexpected heading inside a delta section

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` section containing a heading
  `### Requisito: Modo oscuro` instead of a requirement heading of a
  catalog language
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** an error `delta_unexpected_heading` reports the line
- **AND** its message names the accepted requirement headings,
  `### Requirement:` and `### Exigence :`
- **AND** the section is also reported as empty with the warning
  `delta_section_empty`

#### Scenario: A French requirement heading is no longer unexpected

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` section containing the heading
  `### Exigence : Mode sombre` with a description and a scenario
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** no `delta_unexpected_heading` is reported
- **AND** the `ADDED` operation carries the requirement `Mode sombre`

## Purpose

Let a team write the structure of its specs, deltas and proposals in its own
language: a built-in catalog gives, for each supported language, the form of
every structural keyword codev parses, so that validation, sync and archive
understand a French file as well as an English one.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: A built-in catalog lists the structural keywords of each language

codev SHALL ship a keyword catalog with two languages, `en` and `fr`. For
each language the catalog MUST give one form of every structural keyword
codev parses:

| Keyword | `en` | `fr` |
|---|---|---|
| main spec section | `## Purpose` | `## Objectif` |
| main spec section | `## Requirements` | `## Exigences` |
| requirement heading | `### Requirement: <name>` | `### Exigence : <name>` |
| scenario heading | `#### Scenario: <name>` | `#### Scénario : <name>` |
| delta section | `## ADDED Requirements` | `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` |
| delta section | `## MODIFIED Requirements` | `## Exigences MODIFIÉES` |
| delta section | `## REMOVED Requirements` | `## Exigences SUPPRIMÉES` |
| delta section | `## RENAMED Requirements` | `## Exigences RENOMMÉES` |
| removal labels | `**Reason**`, `**Migration**` | `**Raison**`, `**Migration**` |
| rename lines | `FROM:`, `TO:` | `DE :`, `VERS :` |
| normative keywords | `SHALL`, `MUST` | `DOIT` |
| proposal section | `## What Changes` | `## Changements` |
| proposal section | `## Domains` | `## Domaines` |
| proposal section | `## Release note` | `## Note de version` |

The `en` forms MUST be exactly the keywords codev recognized before the
catalog existed. Values that are identifiers rather than structure — domain
names, release-note categories, the line `None` — are not part of the
catalog and stay in English.

#### Scenario: An English spec is read as before

- **GIVEN** a main spec and a delta written with the English keywords only
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate`, then `codev sync <change>`
- **THEN** the findings and the merged main spec are identical, down to the
  character, to what codev produced before the catalog existed

#### Scenario: A language absent from the catalog is not recognized

- **GIVEN** a delta whose `## ADDED Requirements` section contains a heading
  `### Requisito: Modo oscuro`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** the heading is reported with `delta_unexpected_heading`, since
  no catalog language has that form

### Requirement: Keywords are recognized in every catalog language, whatever the configured language

codev MUST recognize the keywords of every language of the catalog in every
file it parses, independently of the `language:` key of `_codev/config.yaml`.
Changing `language:` SHALL NOT change the outcome of `codev validate` on
existing files.

#### Scenario: A French spec in an English-configured project

- **GIVEN** a project whose configuration has `language: en`
- **AND** a delta written with `## Exigences AJOUTÉES`,
  `### Exigence : Mode sombre`, a description containing `DOIT` and a
  `#### Scénario : Système sombre`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no error is reported for that delta

#### Scenario: An English spec in a French-configured project

- **GIVEN** a project whose configuration has `language: fr`
- **AND** main specs written with the English keywords
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate --all`
- **THEN** the findings are the same as with `language: en`

### Requirement: Keyword matching tolerates case, accents and colon spacing

codev SHALL match a keyword regardless of letter case, SHALL match a French
keyword written with or without its accents, and SHALL accept a French
keyword ending in a colon with or without the space that French typography
puts before it. A heading that lacks the colon entirely MUST NOT be taken for
a requirement or a scenario.

#### Scenario: Unaccented, lowercase delta header

- **GIVEN** a delta containing `## exigences ajoutees` followed by a
  requirement
- **WHEN** the parser reads the delta
- **THEN** the section is an `ADDED` operation carrying that requirement

#### Scenario: Colon with or without a space

- **GIVEN** two deltas, one with `### Exigence : Mode sombre`, the other
  with `### Exigence: Mode sombre`
- **WHEN** the parser reads them
- **THEN** both carry a requirement named `Mode sombre`

#### Scenario: Heading without a colon

- **GIVEN** an `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` section containing the heading
  `### Exigence Mode sombre`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** the heading is reported with `delta_unexpected_heading`
- **AND** no requirement named `Mode sombre` is extracted

### Requirement: Each spec file has a keyword language

The keyword language of a main spec or delta SHALL be the language of its
first structural heading — a main spec section, a delta section, a
requirement or a scenario heading — read outside literal zones. A keyword
whose form is the same in several languages, such as `**Migration**`, MUST
NOT decide the language. A file with no structural heading has the keyword
language `en`.

#### Scenario: A French main spec

- **GIVEN** a main spec starting with `## Objectif`, then `## Exigences`
- **WHEN** codev determines its keyword language
- **THEN** the keyword language is `fr`

#### Scenario: The first heading decides

- **GIVEN** a delta whose first structural heading is
  `## MODIFIED Requirements`, followed further down by
  `## Exigences SUPPRIMÉES`
- **WHEN** codev determines its keyword language
- **THEN** the keyword language is `en`

### Requirement: Proposal sections are found under their name in any catalog language

Wherever codev reads a section of a proposal — the domains, the release note,
the change bullets used as a changelog fallback — it MUST find that section
under its heading in any catalog language. When a proposal carries the same
section under two languages, codev SHALL read the first one in the file.

#### Scenario: French Domains and Release note

- **GIVEN** an active change whose proposal has `## Domaines` with the line
  `- [x] migration`, and `## Note de version` with
  `- Added: un mode sombre.`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>` then, once archived,
  `codev changelog`
- **THEN** validation reports no `domains_*` nor `release_note_*` finding
  for that proposal
- **AND** `codev roles --change <change>` activates the `migration` expert
- **AND** the changelog lists `un mode sombre.` under `Added`

#### Scenario: Unknown domain under a French heading

- **GIVEN** a proposal whose `## Domaines` section contains
  `- [x] sécurité`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** the error `unknown_domain` reports the line, since domain names
  stay in English

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Structural rules beyond the parser

The validator MUST reject as errors the defects that the parser lets
through because they require inspecting the content of a requirement or a
spec: a requirement without a normative keyword of a catalog language —
`SHALL` or `MUST` in English, `DOIT` in French — in its description,
a requirement with no scenario, a main spec with no extractable
requirement.

#### Scenario: Requirement without SHALL or MUST

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` delta with a `### Requirement: X`
  whose descriptive text is "The system does something"
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the file
- **THEN** a finding with code `requirement_no_shall` reports the line of
  the header and names the requirement `X`

#### Scenario: French normative keyword

- **GIVEN** an `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` delta with a `### Exigence : X`
  whose descriptive text is "Le système DOIT conserver le thème choisi"
  and which has a scenario
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the file
- **THEN** no `requirement_no_shall` finding is reported

#### Scenario: French requirement without a normative keyword

- **GIVEN** an `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` delta with a `### Exigence : X`
  whose descriptive text is "Le système conserve le thème"
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the file
- **THEN** a finding with code `requirement_no_shall` reports the line of
  the header, names the requirement `X`, and names `DOIT` among the
  accepted keywords

#### Scenario: Requirement with no scenario at all

- **GIVEN** an `## ADDED Requirements` delta with a `### Requirement: Y`
  followed by its descriptive text but no `#### Scenario:`
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the file
- **THEN** a finding with code `requirement_no_scenario` reports the line
  of the requirement

#### Scenario: Main spec with no requirement

- **GIVEN** a main spec `_codev/specs/x/spec.md` with `## Purpose`
  but whose `## Requirements` is empty
- **WHEN** the validator inspects the spec
- **THEN** a finding with code `spec_no_requirement` reports that the spec
  has no extractable requirement

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: A file mixing keyword languages is warned

The validator SHALL report a warning `mixed_keyword_languages` for a main
spec or a delta whose structural keywords belong to more than one catalog
language, at the line of the first keyword that is not in the file's keyword
language. A keyword whose form is the same in several languages MUST NOT
count as a mix. The warning MUST NOT make `codev validate` fail, except
under `--strict`, like any other warning.

#### Scenario: English requirement heading in a French delta

- **GIVEN** a delta starting with `## Exigences AJOUTÉES` and containing a
  `### Requirement: Mode sombre` heading at line 7
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a warning `mixed_keyword_languages` reports line 7
- **AND** the requirement `Mode sombre` is still validated and merged
- **AND** the command exits with code 0

#### Scenario: A shared keyword is not a mix

- **GIVEN** a French delta whose `## Exigences SUPPRIMÉES` section uses
  `**Raison**` and `**Migration**`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `mixed_keyword_languages` warning is reported

#### Scenario: A delta and its main spec in different languages

- **GIVEN** an English delta that modifies a French main spec
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `mixed_keyword_languages` warning is reported, since each file
  uses a single keyword language
